title: Lacrimal apparatus : Anatomy, Watering eye and Dry eye

questions.q: Tears are classified under secretion and ___.
questions.exp: Tears -> Secretion and Drainage. (Book p215)

questions.q: Main lacrimal gland is divided by levator palpebrae superioris (a) into: 1) Orbital part (3) 2) Palpebral part (4) ... A) Superior  B) Inferior
questions.exp: Main lacrimal gland Divided by levator palpebrae superioris (a) -> Orbital part (3) Superior Palpebral part (4) Inferior -> main excretory ducts (5). (Book p215)

questions.q: Function of the main lacrimal gland is:
questions.exp: Main gland Function : Reflex tear secretion. (Book p215)

questions.q: Accessory lacrimal glands of Krause & Wolfring are located and function as:
opts: Located in fornix (b/w sclera & palpebral conjunctiva) – Basal tear secretions
questions.exp: Accessory glands of Krause & Wolfring : Located in fornix (b/w sclera & palpebral conjunctiva). Function : Basal tear secretions. (Book p215)

questions.q: Parasympathetic innervation of lacrimal gland has secretomotor function. Its centre is:
questions.exp: Parasympathetic innervation : Secretomotor function. Centre : Superior salivary nucleus in pons. (Book p215)

questions.q: Trace the parasympathetic pathway to lacrimal gland: Superior salivary nucleus -> Greater superficial petrosal N (branch of facial N) -> Pterygopalatine ganglion -> ___ -> Lacrimal gland.
opts: Zygomatic N. (Branch of maxillary branch of trigeminal N)
questions.exp: Pre-ganglionic N : Greater superficial petrosal N. (Branch of facial N.) Ganglion : Pterygopalatine. Post ganglionic N. : Zygomatic N. (Branch of maxillary branch of trigeminal N.) Stimulates Lacrimal gland -> Secretion. (Book p215)

questions.q: Sympathetic innervation of lacrimal gland has:
questions.exp: Sympathetic innervation : Inhibitory function. (Book p215)

questions.q: Drainage pathway : Puncta (1) : upper & lower -> Canaliculi : upper (2) & Lower (3) -> Lacrimal sac (4) -> ___ (5) opens in inferior meatus of nose (6).
questions.exp: DRAINAGE Puncta (1) upper & lower -> Canaliculi upper (2) & Lower (3) -> Lacrimal sac (4) -> Nasolacrimal duct - NLD (5) opens in inferior meatus of nose (6). Opening of NLD guarded by valve of Hasner. m/c block in congenital dacryocystitis. (Book p216)

questions.q: Lacrimal sac is surrounded by orbicularis oculi; on blinking it facilitates drainage. The opening of NLD is guarded by:
questions.exp: Opening of NLD guarded by valve of Hasner. m/c block in congenital dacryocystitis. Lacrimal sac Surrounded by orbicularis oculi On blinking -> NLD. (Book p216)

questions.q: Watering of eye — 1) Hyperlacrimation  2) Epiphora … A) Blockage of drainage  B) ↑ tear secretion (Emotional stress, Inflammation)
questions.exp: Watering of eye Hyperlacrimation -> ↑ tear secretion Emotional stress Inflammation ; Epiphora -> Blockage of drainage. (Book p216)

questions.q: Causes of hyperlacrimation listed are:
questions.exp: Hyperlacrimation -> ↑ tear secretion Emotional stress Inflammation. (Book p216)

questions.q: Instruments for testing watering eye include:
opts: Nettleship punctum dilator + Bowman's probe with 26G bent cannula
Only Schirmer strip with Whatman's paper for dry eye
Only Goldmann tonometer for intraocular pressure
Only keratometer for corneal curvature measurement
questions.exp: Instruments : Nettleship punctum dilator 26G bent needle cannula; Bowman's lacrimal probe. (Book p216)

questions.q: Procedure of syringing : Puncta dilated -> Blunt tip of 26G needle inserted into puncta & canaliculi -> Saline injection -> If fluid flows into nose & throat, it indicates:
questions.exp: Syringing : If Fluid flows into nose & throat -> Patent drainage system. If Regurgitation -> Obstruction/blockage. (Book p216)

questions.q: During syringing, regurgitation of fluid occurs. Next step is probing : Hard stop indicates ___, Soft stop indicates ___.
opts: Hard stop NLD blockage; Soft stop Lacrimal sac/Canaliculi block
Hard stop canalicular block; Soft stop NLD blockage
questions.exp: Regurgitation -> Obstruction -> Probing -> Hard stop NLD blockage; Soft stop Lacrimal sac/Canaliculi block. Patent system possibilities : Hypersecretion, Lacrimal pump failure, Partial obstruction -> Jones dye test. (Book p216)

questions.q: When syringing shows fluid flows into nose & throat (patent system) but watering persists, categories are Hypersecretion, Lacrimal pump failure, Partial obstruction – all differentiated by:
questions.exp: Patent drainage system possibilities : Hypersecretion, Lacrimal pump failure, Partial obstruction -> Jones dye test. (Book p216)

questions.q: Jones dye test I : 2% fluorescein dye injected into conjunctival sac, cotton placed at opening of NLD. If cotton bud stains with dye, interpretation is:
opts: Jones dye test I Positive -> Hypersecretion
Jones dye test I Negative -> Hypersecretion
Jones dye test I Positive -> NLD blockage
Jones dye test I Negative -> Complete obstruction
questions.exp: Jones dye test I : If Cotton bud stains -> Jones dye test I Positive -> Hypersecretion. If No staining -> Jones dye test I Negative -> proceed to Jones dye test 2. (Book p217)

questions.q: Jones dye test II : Residual fluorescein is washed out by irrigation. If bud stains thereafter, it indicates:
opts: Partial obstruction of NLD – Jones dye test 2 Positive
questions.exp: Jones dye test 2 : If Bud stains -> Jones dye test 2 Positive -> Partial obstruction of NLD. (Book p217)

questions.q: Jones dye test I Negative, Jones dye test II Negative (no staining of bud after irrigation). Differential diagnoses and next step are:
opts: Only NLD blockage; treat with antibiotics
Lacrimal pump failure OR Partial obstruction of canaliculi – Differentiated by Dacryocystography (DCG)
questions.exp: If Jones 2 Negative -> Lacrimal pump failure vs Partial obstruction of canaliculi -> Differentiated by Dacryocystography (DCG). (Book p217)

questions.q: Dacryocystitis is inflammation of the ___.
questions.exp: DACRYOCYSTITIS Inflammation of lacrimal sac. (Book p217)

questions.q: Congenital dacryocystitis presents as c/o watering since birth, cause Non-canalization of NLD, m/c site of occlusion:
questions.exp: Congenital : Presentation C/o watering since birth. Cause Non-canalization of NLD. m/c site Valve of Hasner. (Book p217)

questions.q: Management of congenital dacryocystitis by age — Match : 9-12 months vs >1 yr vs >4 yrs:
opts: 9-12 months Syringing, >1 yr Probing, >4 yrs DCR
questions.exp: Rx : Lacrimal sac massage + Topical antibiotics (Tobramycin, erythromycin). 9-12 months Syringing. >1 yr Probing. >4 yrs Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR). (Book p217)

questions.q: Initial conservative treatment for congenital dacryocystitis includes:
opts: Immediate DCR surgery at birth for all neonates
Systemic steroids alone for anti-inflammatory effect
Topical steroids only without antibiotics or massage
questions.exp: Rx : Lacrimal sac massage + Topical antibiotics (Tobramycin, erythromycin). (Book p217)

questions.q: Acquired dacryocystitis cause and treatment:
opts: Cause Streptococcus hemolyticus, Rx Oral antibiotics, DCR if fistula (+)
questions.exp: Acquired : Cause Streptococcus hemolyticus. Rx : Oral antibiotics, DCR If fistula (+). (Book p217)

questions.q: Tumours of lacrimal gland — Pleomorphic adenoma (Benign) vs Adenoid cystic carcinoma (malignant) share which clinical displacement?
opts: Displacement of eye upwards and laterally
Displacement of eye downwards and medially d/t location of lacrimal gland
questions.exp: TUMOURS OF LACRIMAL GLAND Pleomorphic adenoma Benign, Adenoid cystic carcinoma malignant -> Displacement of eye downwards and medially d/t location of lacrimal gland. (Book p218)

questions.q: Tear film layers — Innermost, Middle, Outermost correspond to:
opts: Innermost Lipid (meibomian) , Middle Aqueous, Outermost Mucin
Innermost Mucin (Goblet cells), Middle Aqueous (Lacrimal glands), Outermost Lipid (Meibomian gland) – Prevents evaporation of aqueous
Innermost Aqueous, Middle Lipid, Outermost Mucin
questions.exp: TEAR FILM Innermost mucin (Goblet cells), Middle Aqueous (Lacrimal glands), Outermost Lipid (Meibomian gland) Prevents evaporation of aqueous. Plus Corneal epithelium with microvilli. (Book p218)

questions.q: Which layer prevents evaporation of aqueous?
questions.exp: Outermost Lipid (Meibomian gland) Prevents evaporation of aqueous. (Book p218)

questions.q: Match dry eye disorder type — 1) Aqueous deficiency  2) Lipid deficiency  3) Mucin deficiency … A) Keratoconjunctivitis sicca Eg Sjogren syndrome  B) Evaporative dry eye – meibomian gland disease, Contact lens wearer  C) Vit A deficiency
questions.exp: DISORDERS Table : Aqueous deficiency AKA Keratoconjunctivitis sicca Eg Sjogren syndrome; Lipid deficiency AKA Evaporative dry eye meibomian gland disease Contact lens wearer; Mucin deficiency Vit A deficiency. (Book p218)

questions.q: Schirmer test is a quantitative test to measure tear production using:
questions.exp: Schirmer test : Quantitative test to measure tear production. Uses Whatman's filter paper No. 41. (Book p218)

questions.q: Procedure: Strip inserted in lower fornix for 5 mins. Length of wet strip >15 mm is Normal, <10 mm is:
questions.exp: Procedure Inserted in lower fornix 5 mins Length >15 mm Normal <10 mm Dry eye. Images Whatman's filter paper Schirmer test. (Book p218)

questions.q: TBUT (Tear Film Break-up Time) steps: 2% Fluorescein instilled -> Illuminated with blue light -> Interval between blink & appearance of 1st spot of dryness of cornea. If <10 sec, indicates:
questions.exp: TBUT : <10 sec Mucin deficiency. Dry spot at a particular location -> Corneal disease. (Book p219)

questions.q: During TBUT, a dry spot appears at a particular location repeatedly. This suggests:
questions.exp: TBUT Dry spot at a particular location -> Corneal disease. (Book p219)

questions.q: Phenol red thread test uses thread impregnated with phenol red dye which is yellow in colour and turns red with tears. Placed in lower fornix. Interpretation:
questions.exp: Phenol red thread test : Yellow + tears -> Red. <6 mm Dry eye >15 mm Normal. Thread placed in lower fornix. (Book p219)

questions.q: A phenol red thread shows 4 mm wetting, TBUT 7 sec, Schirmer 8 mm. Consistent with:
questions.exp: Phenol <6 Dry eye, TBUT <10 mucin deficiency, Schirmer <10 Dry eye. (Book p219)
